decisions.title: Deployment model for v1
decisions.question: Where should activeDIQ v1 run for the customers we want to win from ManageEngine?
decisions.context:
Most ManageEngine AD customers run on-premises on Windows Server and expect an installer. We can start there, ship a container for Linux-first shops, or host it ourselves.

- This is expensive to reverse: it shapes packaging, upgrades, support and the security story.
- Read the [deployment options brief](knowledge/development/architecture/deployment-options.md) for the cost of each path.

**Blocked until you answer:** packaging and the installer work.

options.label: On-prem installer first
options.summary: Windows service plus web console, installed next to the domain. Container follows in M3.
pros: Matches how ManageEngine customers deploy today
Domain-joined, so no inbound firewall holes to AD

options.label: Self-hosted container
options.summary: A container image plus a small on-prem connector agent.
cons: Many AD admins are not container-ready

options.label: Hosted SaaS with on-prem connector
options.summary: We run the console; a connector in the customer network talks to AD.
cons: Tier-0 data leaves the building: a hard sell and a heavy compliance load
Needs multi-tenancy in the first migration

decisions.rationale: It is the shortest path to a credible demo for the buyers we are targeting, and it keeps Tier-0 data inside their network.

decisions.title: Default table density for the console
decisions.question: Should lists and audit tables default to comfortable (40 px rows) or compact (32 px)?
decisions.context: Admins scan thousands of rows. The factory default is **comfortable with a compact toggle**, but this is a taste call. Both previews use the same seeded users.

options.label: Comfortable
options.summary: 40 px rows. Calmer, easier to scan, fewer rows per screen.

options.label: Compact
options.summary: 32 px rows. More data per screen, closer to what power admins expect.

decisions.rationale: Our buyers are admins who live in these tables all day. The toggle covers everyone else.

decisions.title: Audit log is hash-chained from the first release
decisions.question: The factory chose a tamper-evident audit log for v1. You can veto.
decisions.context: Audit events are appended with a hash of the previous event, so edits or deletions are detectable. It costs little now and is painful to retrofit.

options.label: Hash-chained append-only log
options.summary: Each event carries the hash of its predecessor; a verifier job flags breaks.

decisions.rationale: Audit credibility is part of how we displace incumbents. Retrofitting integrity onto existing rows is not honest.

decisions.title: Module scope for v1
decisions.question: Which modules ship in v1?
decisions.context: Directory management, reports and audit are the core. Self-service password reset and MFA are separate products in the incumbent suite.

answer.note: Core only. Revisit SSPR after the first partner demo.

decisions.title: Navigation label: "Directory" or "Objects"
decisions.question: What should the primary nav call the user, group and OU browser?

decisions.title: Preferred report export formats
decisions.question: Which export formats first?
decisions.rationale: Withdrawn: the reporting spec already settled this from the research corpus (CSV, XLSX and PDF).

decisions.title: Branches and commits follow ticket ids
decisions.context: Branches are named `factory/T-0000`; commit subjects start with the ticket id.

decisions.title: Audit views show times in UTC by default
decisions.context: Audit and detail views show absolute UTC time.

answer.note: Use the admin’s local zone and always show the zone label.

actions.detail:

# ADR-0002: audit event schema

> **Fixture data.** This page exists only to preview the board. It is not real research or a real decision.

## Status

proposed. It becomes **accepted** when the schema fitness function runs in CI.

## Decision

An audit event is immutable and self-describing:

```json
{
  "id": "01J9Z6...",
  "ts": "2026-10-02T14:30:00Z",
  "actor": { "type": "user", "sid": "S-1-5-21-..." },
  "target": { "dn": "CN=Jo Doe,OU=Staff,DC=corp,DC=example", "guid": "..." },
  "change": [{ "attr": "mail", "old": "a@x", "new": "b@x" }],
  "source_dc": "dc01.corp.example",
  "correlation_id": "..."
}
```

## Consequences

- Events are **append-only**; each carries the hash of its predecessor (see the factory notice on hash chaining).
- Reads are paged by cursor; see [the paging contract](../architecture/map.md).
- Sensitive attribute values are redacted by policy, never silently dropped.

## Alternatives considered

- Plain rows with a trigger: simpler, but integrity cannot be proven.
- Store the raw directory event: couples us to the log format.
